contract: Same executable runs native plaintext legacy WebSocket and encrypted WebTransport. Fixed clients. Three rotated twelve-second process repeats per reliable workload, serialized. Capacity: one pair, 100000 users, 6250 rooms of 16, 400000 verified self-route deliveries. Kernel counters separate from RSS. Shared desktop host.

server.scope: Process-owned connected TCP sockets or bound UDP sockets, filtered by the requested ports. skmem fields are separate counters, not an additive total. Buffer limits are not allocations. Slab object estimate excludes slab overhead, protocol buffers, route/conntrack state and other kernel resources. TIME_WAIT port matches have no live fd and are reported separately. This is not complete kernel memory accounting.

websocket.scope: Diagnostic allocator, all five gates passed, exact executable/profile hashes and bucket totals validated. Not ordinary RSS or timing. WT capture was taken immediately before the commit with identical executable and traffic workload.

webtransport.scope: Diagnostic allocator, all five gates passed, exact executable/profile hashes and bucket totals validated. Not ordinary RSS or timing. WT capture was taken immediately before the commit with identical executable and traffic workload.

kernel_scope: Read-only slab sizes: TCP2432B, UDP1344B on this kernel. 100000 TCP socket objects estimate243200000B versus one UDP1344B. Not complete kernel memory; skmem counters are not an additive total, buffer limits are not allocations, and TIME_WAIT port matches have no live fd. All socket snapshots are outside offered traffic phase.
scope_limits: One capacity pair does not establish statistical timing confidence.
RTT histogram p50/p99 values are bucket upper bounds, not exact percentiles.
Native WebSocket is plaintext while WebTransport is encrypted, as required by the retained native baseline contract.
Do not infer allocator leaks from high RSS after zero application gauges.
Profiles support focusing on user-space driving/wake/dispatch/timer work but do not prove a particular scheduler change will help.
Recent datagram/freshness/browser acceptance is recorded in docs/reports/webtransport-handshake-spans-2026-10-22.json; this run refreshes native reliable/capacity parity only.
Capacity gate_wall_seconds includes phase-control and diagnostic work; use the fixed client offered-phase counts/rates for traffic throughput, not gate-wall division.
next_experiment: Prototype worker-grouped Quinn connection drivers while retaining independent UDP ingress. Test whether grouping driver readiness reduces per-recipient scheduling/wakeup cost and per-connection task overhead. Preserve protocol engine behavior, individual wake registration, FIFO, budgets, cancellation and worker fairness. Earlier application/driver co-driving rejection remains distinct evidence; do not repeat that prototype unchanged.
